questions.question: What is commercial farming? How is it different from subsistence farming?
questions.expected_answer: Commercial farming is farming mainly to sell crops and animals for a profit. Commercial farms are usually large, use machines and paid workers, and often specialise in a few crops or animals. Subsistence farming is farming mainly to feed your own family, on small farms with simple tools and family labour.

questions.question: Name three ways commercial farmers use machines, workers or water.
questions.expected_answer: Tractors pull ploughs and planters; combine harvesters cut and thresh the crop; sprayers spread fertiliser; paid workers drive machines, fix them and pick fruit; irrigation brings water to crops by pipes, canals or sprinklers.

questions.question: Describe the journey of maize from a commercial farm to the shops.
questions.expected_answer: The maize is harvested and taken by truck to silos, where it is dried and stored. It is sold and sent by train or truck to mills, where it is ground into maize meal and packed into bags for shops. Some goes to factories and some is exported by ship.
